synopsis: ISO 15998 formerly covered functional safety of electronic machine-control systems on earth-moving machinery; ISO 15998:2008 and ISO/TS 15998-2:2012 were withdrawn on 14 June 2022 and replaced by ISO 19014 [f15250, f2344, f15251]. A legacy-reference tension remains: ISO 16001:2017 still cites ISO 15998 for environmental conditions, while allowing ISO 19014-3 as an alternative; readers encountering supplier references to ISO 15998 should request the ISO 19014 equivalent [f2345, f15252, f15253, f15257]. ISO 16001 requires electromagnetic compatibility to ISO 13766, meaning electronics must neither disrupt other equipment through radio interference nor be disrupted by external interference [f2414, f15254, f15255]. EMC matters for automatic braking because brake requests travel over an electronic network and radar shares radio space; MOSH includes EMC testing in its TRL4 laboratory phase, and an on-road example identifies radio-frequency coexistence as one reason a factory emergency brake was disabled [f15258, f15256, f15259].
